lines.trans: Hello, Samsonov.
I have a meeting with Putin today.
It is a big secret, no one should know.
What are you saying? What Putin?
We only have one Putin in the country.
Did you come for your things?
How are you feeling right now, Vanya?
I feel bad, really terrible.
I need to prepare for the meeting urgently.
Are you joking, Samson? Is that a defense mechanism?
No, I am a true people's candidate!
Do not cover up your grief with bravado.
We are worrying about you very much.
There is no need to worry about me!
Alright, get out of here, I am very busy.

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('big, large').

examples.text: Аракелян просит время. Сумма очень большая.
examples.trans: Arakelyan is asking for more time. The sum is very large.

meanings.note: Pretended confidence. Common feminine noun meaning 'bravado, swagger' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не надо прикрывать своё горе бравадой.
examples.trans: Do not cover up your grief with bravado.

examples.text: Вся его смелость — это просто пустая бравада.
examples.trans: All his bravery is just empty bravado.

meanings.note: + prepositional (where). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.
+ accusative (where to). Core Russian prep meaning 'in, into' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Plural 'вещи'. Common feminine noun meaning 'thing' in everyday Russian.
Plural 'вещи'. Common feminine noun meaning 'thing' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.
In 'до встречи' = until we meet. Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'треча'). Common feminine noun meaning 'meeting' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Решается ваш вопрос, Клавдия Викторовна! Вы не видите, у меня встреча?
examples.trans: Your question is being sorted out, Klavdia Viktorovna! Can't you see I have a meeting?

meanings.note: ends a conversation or an order: 'Всё, свободен' = that's all, you can go
At the start of a sentence. Core Russian pron meaning 'everything, all; that's it' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: Deep emotional suffering. Common neuter noun meaning 'grief, sorrow' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Не надо прикрывать своё горе бравадой.
examples.trans: Do not cover up your grief with bravado.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: + infinitive; agrees with the subject: должна (f)
Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'лжен'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('must, should; owe').

examples.text: Жадность, Паша, должна быть умеренная. Комнатной температуры.
examples.trans: Greed, Pasha, should be moderate. Room temperature.

meanings.note: Спасибо за + accusative. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.
+ instrumental. Core Russian prep meaning 'for; behind' in everyday speech.

Of a person: я занят = I'm busy. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'нятый'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('busy; occupied, taken').
of a place: здесь занято = it's occupied

Serving to protect or defend. Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'щитный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('protective, defense').

examples.text: Ты шутишь, Самсон? Это защитная реакция?
examples.trans: Are you joking, Samson? Is that a defense mechanism?

meanings.note: to one person you call ты; здравствуйте is the polite form; the first в is silent
A fact or a person. Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to know'.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: + dative. Core Russian prep meaning 'to, towards' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: There's someone here to see you.

examples.text: Аркадий Борисович, извините, тут к вам человек.
examples.trans: Arkady Borisovich, I'm sorry, there's a man here to see you.

meanings.note: Question word. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.
Как вы знаете = as you know. Core Russian adv meaning 'how; as' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: In questions. Core Russian det meaning 'what; what a' in everyday speech.
in exclamations: какой грязный! = how dirty!

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: In an election or for a job. From Latin 'candidatus' ('clothed in white toga', worn by office-seekers in ancient Rome).

examples.trans: He is a candidate for mayor.

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place

meanings.en: other forms: нас (gen/acc), нам (dat), нами (instr), нас (prep)
meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'we' in everyday speech.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.en: must, need to, it is necessary
meanings.note: Надо + infinitive. Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: We need to do even more.

meanings.note: Belonging to the people. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'родный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('people's, public, folk').

Народная песня = folk song. Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'родный'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('people's, public, folk').

examples.text: За народными деньгами иди к народу.
examples.trans: For the people's money, go to the people.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').
Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'стоящий'). Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('real, genuine').

examples.text: Ваня, да пойми ты наконец! Это настоящий успех.
examples.trans: Vanya, understand at last! This is real success.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
one direction, now; 'Неси!' = Bring (it)!

examples.trans: Yulia, bring a pen and a piece of paper.

meanings.note: + genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
+ genitive. Core Russian part meaning 'no; there isn't' in everyday speech.
needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.en: it is necessary, one needs to
meanings.note: + dative of the person + infinitive: мне нужно позвонить

examples.trans: I need to make a call.

examples.text: Мне нужно позвонить губернатору. Дай телефон.
examples.trans: I need to call the governor. Give me a phone.

meanings.note: agrees in gender and case with the noun
Core Russian num meaning 'one' in everyday speech.

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Locative / directional adverb. Prefix 'от-' ('away from, off') marks separation, completion, or response (stem 'сюда').

examples.text: Я выйду отсюда через две недели. Я решу все ваши проблемы.
examples.trans: I'll be out of here in two weeks. I'll solve all your problems.

meanings.note: With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.
With verbs: очень люблю. Core Russian adv meaning 'very, very much' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: I love our town very much.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.

переживать.gloss: to worry, to fret; to go through

meanings.note: Intransitive or за + accusative. Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'живать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry, to fret; to go through', paired with 'пережить'.

Prefix 'пере-' denotes crossing over, repeating, or exceeding a limit (stem 'живать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to worry, to fret; to go through', paired with 'пережить'.

examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that?
Don't worry, everything will be fine.

examples.text: Что вы так переживаете? Самсонов всё, он себя закопал.
examples.trans: Why are you worrying like that? Samsonov is finished, he buried himself.

meanings.note: Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.
Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Послушайте, а можно в другое место? Здесь плохо пахнет.
examples.trans: Listen, could we go somewhere else? It smells bad in here.

meanings.en: to prepare, to get oneself ready
meanings.note: For an event or test. Prefix 'под-' ('under, up to') indicates approaching or supporting from below (stem 'готовиться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to prepare, to get ready', paired with 'готовиться'.

examples.trans: Get ready and go to the debate.

examples.text: Успокоить жену! Подготовиться и поехать на дебаты.
examples.trans: Calm your wife down! Get ready and go to the debate.

examples.text: Мне нужно срочно подготовиться к встрече.
examples.trans: I need to prepare for the meeting urgently.

meanings.note: On foot, once. Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to come, to arrive', paired with 'приходить'.

examples.trans: Security will be here any moment.

examples.text: Не надо, Самсон. Сейчас придёт охрана.
examples.trans: Don't, Samson. Security will be here any second.

meanings.note: To hide under a pretense. Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'крывать'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to cover up, to conceal', paired with 'прикрыть'.

examples.text: Не надо прикрывать своё горе бравадой.
examples.trans: Do not cover up your grief with bravado.

examples.text: Он всегда прикрывает своих друзей в трудную минуту.
examples.trans: He always covers for his friends in a tough moment.

meanings.note: International noun in '-ция' (from Latin '-tio'), feminine declension. Common feminine noun meaning 'reaction' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The reaction is positive. People like it.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Reflexive; no nominative. Core Russian pron meaning 'oneself' in everyday speech.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: The г sounds like в. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'егодня').

examples.text: Виктор Степанович, сегодня никак не могу.
examples.trans: Viktor Stepanovich, I really can't today.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ейчас').

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Adverb of degree. Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'ильно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: The wind is blowing hard outside.

examples.text: Я так два года потеряла. Любила так сильно!
examples.trans: I lost two years like that. I loved him so much!

meanings.en: urgently, right away; predicative: it is urgent
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'рочно'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.trans: I need to make a phone call urgently.

examples.text: Павел Юрьевич, это срочно! Я должна вам сказать.
examples.trans: Pavel Yuryevich, this is urgent! I must tell you.

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'трана'). Common feminine noun meaning 'country' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you!

examples.text: Над тобой вся страна смеётся! Все видели, как ты из окна летел.
examples.trans: The whole country is laughing at you! Everyone saw you fly out the window.

meanings.note: адвокатская тайна = attorney-client privilege

examples.text: Как? Ты?! А как же адвокатская тайна?
examples.trans: How? You?! What about lawyer-client secrecy?

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Уходи! = Go away!. Prefix 'у-' marks departure, removal, or successful completion (stem 'ходить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to leave, to go away', paired with 'уйти'.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to joke', paired with 'пошутить'.

examples.text: Шутишь? Правда, скажи, где деньги? Меня наняли.

points at something: это моё = that's mine
Linking word: главное — это народ. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

meanings.note: Case forms. Core Russian pron meaning 'this, that; it is' in everyday speech.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.en: other forms: меня (gen/acc), мне (dat), мной (instr), мне (prep)

на днях = in the next few days, or the other day

examples.trans: I'll call in the next few days.
Any day now, on the website.
